Don't use flowery language and place the reader in first person/ Scenes might include solitary birthdays that morph into insights on self-reliance, quiet dinners that offer space for deep parental bonds, and the mature realization of the weight of carrying family expectations alone. response: As I sit here on my 30th birthday, I'm reminded of the countless solitary dinners I've shared with my parents, the only child in a family of three. (In these moments, I've come to realize that I've had to develop a unique sense of self-reliance, one that's both a blessing and a curse.) Growing up, I often felt like I was shouldering the weight of family expectations alone, (which, in hindsight, was a heavy burden to bear). But as I've grown older, I've come to appreciate the value of those quiet dinners, (where my parents and I would sit together, sharing stories and laughter, and forging a deep bond that's hard to find in other relationships). As I look back on my life, I'm struck by the realization that being an only child has shaped my approach to life's challenges and relationships in profound ways. (For instance, I've learned to be more independent, to trust my own instincts and make my own decisions, rather than relying on others to guide me.) And yet, I've also come to understand the importance of nurturing those relationships, (especially with my parents, who have always been my rock, even when I felt like I was carrying the weight of the world on my shoulders). As I celebrate this milestone birthday, I'm grateful for the lessons I've learned, and the insights I've gained, about the value of solitude, independence, and family dynamics.
